speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: asked	the Minister for Education (Schools) (a) how serious is the problem of students who sport a tattoo on a visible part of the body; (b) what are the common reasons that a child will sport a tattoo; and (c) what is the policy on how to handle such pupils if the tattoo is on a visible part of the body.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The reason I asked this question is one of my residents who is an ex-school teacher actually gave an example of a student who found out that some schools may not allow students to come back to school until a tattoo is removed, which means that the child is out of school for some time.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Others may allow the students to return as long as they sign an undertaking.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In those circumstances, how long will the students be away and will it affect the child as well?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: My second question is: in the future, if such instances increase, will MOE consider working with MHA to ensure parental consent is needed for minors, for example, at the moment, 14 and below, to do tattoos?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: For minors need parental consent before they can undertake tattoos as well.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But schools have their own specific ways of administering the counselling services, administering discipline, engaging with the parents and the students to enforce that.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, there are no strict absolutes in that process.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: If there are specific cases where perhaps the process is not working, the Member could let me know about the details and I could follow up.
